title: Continuous Subarray Sum
description: Check if an array has a contiguous subarray of size at least 2 that sums to a multiple of k.
pseudocode:
1. rem_map = {0: -1}
2. running_sum = 0
3. for i, num in enumerate(nums):
4.   running_sum += num
5.   rem = running_sum % k
6.   if rem in rem_map:
7.     if i - rem_map[rem] >= 2: return True
8.   else: rem_map[rem] = i

steps.note: Initialize remainder map with 0 at index -1
Remainder 5 found at index 0. Diff = 2 - 0 = 2. Subarray [2, 4] found.

fullDescription:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if nums has a good subarray or false otherwise.

A good subarray is a subarray where:

  • its length is at least two, and
  • the sum of the elements of the subarray is a multiple of k.

Note that:

  • A subarray is a contiguous part of the array.
  • An integer x is a multiple of k if there exists an integer n such that x = n * k. 0 is always a multiple of k.

 

Example 1:

Input: nums = [23,2,4,6,7], k = 6
Output: true
Explanation: [2, 4] is a continuous subarray of size 2 whose elements sum up to 6.

Example 2:

Input: nums = [23,2,6,4,7], k = 6
Output: true
Explanation: [23, 2, 6, 4, 7] is an continuous subarray of size 5 whose elements sum up to 42.
42 is a multiple of 6 because 42 = 7 * 6 and 7 is an integer.

Example 3:

Input: nums = [23,2,6,4,7], k = 13
Output: false

 

Constraints:

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 105
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 109
  • 0 <= sum(nums[i]) <= 231 - 1
  • 1 <= k <= 231 - 1
